newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec party says sovereignty remains goal.
newsitem.headline: Quebec party says sovereignty remains goal.

text.p: The Bloc Quebecois, the official opposition in the Parliament, declared on Friday that independence from Canada remains its goal even if it would make jobs its priority in the near future.

"The Bloc Quebecois is determined to show that the Quebec people's move towards sovereignty is a noble undertaking and that Quebec is devoted to becoming sovereign," Bloc leader Michel Gauthier said in a statement.
He said the Bloc was determined to prevent the federal government from penalising Quebec on the grounds that Quebec was trying to become sovereign.
Gauthier argued that as long as Quebeckers sends C$30 billion (US$21.8 billion) in taxes, they have the right to their fair share.

He added that employment would be the Bloc's priority in the upcoming months: "We are going to question (Prime Minister) Jean Chretien's government hard in order to ensure that it respects its commitments to create jobs and to revive the economy."
The Bloc had campaigned in a referendum on Quebec sovereignty that narrowly failed last October.
